newsitem.title: UK: Silver fixes at 18-month low, gold holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Silver fixes at 18-month low, gold holds steady.

text.p: Silver fixed at an 18-month low in nervous trading on Friday after an overnight sell-off sent prices spiralling below the key $5.00 an ounce level.
Analysts said the silver market looked likely to continue plumbing the depths of the downside.
"It broke through an important trend line going back three years last night and that's knocked the confidence out of the market quite a lot," a dealer said.
Silver fixed at $4.9450 an ounce, compared to $5.0680 on Thursday and the lowest since March 30, 1995.
The sharp drop, initiated in New York by disillusioned investors, proved the market's vulnerability after days of hovering just above $5.00, analysts said.
Gold, by contrast, was holding up above its $382 support level. Bullion fixed at $382.50 an ounce, down just $0.25 from Thursday afternoon.
"Gold has remained remarkably immobile at the moment, which would indicate the market is hugely short," a dealer said. After $382, support was expected to emerge around $380.
But silver was now more susceptible to downside pressure.

"Critical support at 500 cents has been breached and the likelihood is that falls will go considerably further," technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
"The inital target is the 480 cent area but, longer term, 460 cents could well be seen," Gifford added.

A possible well of support, however, may come from silver's oversold status, dealers said. "Funds like selling into weakness and there may be more weakness to come yet," a dealer said. "But the psychology is that if everyone thinks it's going one way, it won't."
The downside also beckoned to the rest of the precious metals, although gold was expected to escape relatively unscathed in the near term.
Like silver, it was oversold and seen unlikely to drift much below $381.50 on Friday, dealers said.
Platinum was slightly weaker in sympathy with silver at $388.25 an ounce, but palladium was $1.20 firmer at $120.75.
